es.B: Ese mismo día se informó al rey del número de los muertos en la ciudadela de Susa.
es.R: Ese día le dijeron al rey cuántas personas habían sido muertas en la fortaleza real de Susa.

fr.L: Ce jour-là, le nombre de ceux qui avaient été tués à Suse la citadelle parvint devant le roi.
fr.B: Ce jour-là même, on rapporta au roi le nombre de ceux qui avaient été tués dans la citadelle de Suse.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, on a dit au roi combien de personnes avaient été tuées dans la forteresse royale de Suse.

sw.L: Siku ile hesabu ya waliouawa katika Shushani ngomeni ikaletwa mbele ya mfalme.
sw.B: Siku hiyo hiyo idadi ya waliouawa katika ngome ya Shushani iliripotiwa kwa mfalme.
sw.R: Siku hiyo mfalme aliambiwa ni watu wangapi waliouawa katika ngome ya kifalme huko Shushani.

vi.L: Ngày hôm ấy, số người bị giết tại thành nội Su-sơ được đem đến trước mặt vua.
vi.B: Ngay ngày hôm ấy, số người bị giết tại thành nội Su-sơ được tâu lên vua.
vi.R: Ngày hôm ấy, người ta báo cho vua biết có bao nhiêu người đã bị giết tại hoàng thành Su-sơ.

ko.L: 그날에 수산 성에서 죽임을 당한 자들의 수가 왕 앞에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 바로 그날 수산 성채에서 죽임을 당한 자들의 수가 왕에게 보고되었다.
ko.R: 그날 왕은 수산 왕궁에서 몇 명이 죽었는지 보고를 받았다.

decisions.choice: came before the king: was reported to him
decisions.reason: To come before the king is to be brought to his notice, as reports and requests are in 1:19 and 9:25.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֗ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֡ה הָרְגוּ֩ הַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְאַבֵּ֜ד חֲמֵ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ וְאֵת֙ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת בְּנֵֽי־הָמָ֔ן בִּשְׁאָ֛ר מְדִינ֥וֹת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ וּמַה־שְּׁאֵֽלָתֵךְ֙ וְיִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֔ךְ וּמַה־בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Esther the queen, in Susa the citadel have killed the Jews and destroyed five hundred men and [the] ten sons of Haman; in [the] rest of [the] provinces of the king what have they done? And what [is] your petition? And it will be given to you. And what [is] your request further? And it will be done.

en.L: And the king said to Queen Esther, "In Susa the citadel the Jews have killed and destroyed 500 men and the ten sons of Haman. In the rest of the king's provinces, what have they done! And what is your petition? It shall be given to you. And what more is your request? It shall be done."
en.B: The king said to Queen Esther, "In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed 500 men and the ten sons of Haman. What must they have done in the rest of the king's provinces! Now what is your petition? It will be granted you. What else do you ask? It will be done."
en.R: The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews have killed 500 men in the royal fortress in Susa, and also Haman's ten sons. They must have killed many more in the rest of my provinces! Now what else do you want? I will give it to you. Tell me what you ask for, and it will be done."

es.L: Y dijo el rey a la reina Ester: «En Susa la ciudadela los judíos han matado y destruido a 500 hombres y a los diez hijos de Amán. ¡En el resto de las provincias del rey, qué habrán hecho! ¿Y cuál [es] tu petición? Y se te concederá. ¿Y cuál [es] además tu solicitud? Y se hará».
es.B: El rey dijo a la reina Ester: «En la ciudadela de Susa los judíos han matado y destruido a 500 hombres y a los diez hijos de Amán. ¡Qué no habrán hecho en el resto de las provincias del rey! Ahora bien, ¿cuál es tu petición? Se te concederá. ¿Qué más pides? Se hará».
es.R: El rey le dijo a la reina Ester: «Los judíos han matado a 500 hombres en la fortaleza real de Susa, y también a los diez hijos de Amán. ¡Cuántos más habrán matado en el resto de mis provincias! Ahora dime, ¿qué más quieres? Te lo daré. Dime lo que pides, y se hará».

fr.L: Et le roi dit à la reine Esther : « À Suse la citadelle, les Juifs ont tué et fait périr 500 hommes et les dix fils de Haman. Dans le reste des provinces du roi, qu’ont-ils fait ! Et quelle [est] ta requête ? Elle te sera accordée. Et quelle [est] encore ta demande ? Elle sera exécutée. »
fr.B: Le roi dit à la reine Esther : « Dans la citadelle de Suse, les Juifs ont tué et fait périr 500 hommes et les dix fils de Haman. Qu’auront-ils fait dans le reste des provinces du roi ! Maintenant, quelle est ta requête ? Elle te sera accordée. Que demandes-tu encore ? Ce sera fait. »
fr.R: Le roi a dit à la reine Esther : « Les Juifs ont tué 500 hommes dans la forteresse royale de Suse, et aussi les dix fils de Haman. Ils ont dû en tuer bien davantage dans le reste de mes provinces ! Maintenant, que veux-tu encore ? Je te le donnerai. Dis-moi ce que tu demandes, et ce sera fait. »

sw.L: Mfalme akamwambia malkia Esta, "Katika Shushani ngomeni Wayahudi wameua na kuangamiza watu 500 na wana kumi wa Hamani. Katika majimbo mengine ya mfalme wamefanya nini! Na haja yako [ni] nini? Nawe utapewa. Na ombi lako zaidi [ni] nini? Nalo litafanyika."
sw.B: Mfalme akamwambia malkia Esta, "Katika ngome ya Shushani Wayahudi wameua na kuangamiza watu 500 na wana kumi wa Hamani. Je, watakuwa wamefanya nini katika majimbo mengine ya mfalme! Sasa haja yako ni nini? Utapewa. Unaomba nini zaidi? Litafanyika."
sw.R: Mfalme akamwambia malkia Esta, "Wayahudi wameua watu 500 katika ngome ya kifalme huko Shushani, na pia wana kumi wa Hamani. Bila shaka wameua wengi zaidi katika majimbo yangu mengine! Sasa unataka nini zaidi? Nitakupa. Niambie unaloomba, nalo litafanyika."

vi.L: Vua nói với hoàng hậu Ê-xơ-tê: "Tại thành nội Su-sơ, người Do Thái đã giết và hủy diệt 500 người cùng mười con trai của Ha-man. Trong các tỉnh còn lại của vua, họ đã làm gì nữa! Và lời thỉnh cầu của nàng là gì? Sẽ được ban cho nàng. Và nàng còn cầu xin gì nữa? Sẽ được làm."
vi.B: Vua phán với hoàng hậu Ê-xơ-tê: "Tại thành nội Su-sơ, người Do Thái đã giết và tiêu diệt 500 người cùng mười con trai của Ha-man. Trong các tỉnh khác của vua, không biết họ còn làm đến đâu! Bây giờ nàng thỉnh cầu điều gì? Điều đó sẽ được ban cho nàng. Nàng còn cầu xin gì nữa? Điều đó sẽ được thực hiện."
vi.R: Vua nói với hoàng hậu Ê-xơ-tê: "Người Do Thái đã giết 500 người tại hoàng thành Su-sơ, và cả mười con trai của Ha-man nữa. Chắc hẳn họ đã giết nhiều hơn nữa trong các tỉnh khác của ta! Bây giờ nàng còn muốn gì nữa? Ta sẽ ban cho nàng. Hãy nói cho ta biết nàng xin gì, và điều đó sẽ được thực hiện."

ko.L: 그리고 왕이 왕후 에스더에게 말했다. "수산 성에서 유대인이 500명과 하만의 열 아들을 죽이고 멸하였소. 왕의 나머지 지방들에서는 그들이 무엇을 하였겠소! 그리고 그대의 소청이 무엇이오? 그대에게 주어질 것이오. 그리고 그대의 요청이 또 무엇이오? 이루어질 것이오."
ko.B: 왕이 왕후 에스더에게 말했다. "수산 성채에서 유대인이 500명과 하만의 열 아들을 죽여 없앴소. 왕의 나머지 지방들에서는 얼마나 많이 죽였겠소! 이제 그대의 소청이 무엇이오? 들어주겠소. 그 밖에 또 무엇을 요청하겠소? 이루어 주겠소."
ko.R: 왕이 왕후 에스더에게 말했다. "유대인이 수산 왕궁에서 500명을 죽였고, 하만의 열 아들도 죽였소. 내 나머지 지방들에서는 훨씬 더 많이 죽였을 것이오! 이제 또 원하는 것이 무엇이오? 주겠소. 무엇을 청하든지 말해 보시오. 다 이루어 주겠소."

decisions.choice: what have they done: an exclamation, not a request for figures
alternatives: a real question: what have they done in the other provinces?
decisions.reason: The question has no answer in the text and the king goes straight on to Esther's wish. It means: if this happened in Susa alone, think how much they have done in the rest of the provinces.

decisions.choice: your petition, your request: the king's words at Esther's earlier feasts
decisions.reason: The king offers again in the same words he used at both of Esther's banquets (5:6; 7:2). Then she asked for her life; now he asks what more she wants.

decisions.choice: my provinces
decisions.reason: The king speaks of himself as "the king"; Readable says "my" so the reader does not wonder who is meant.

source.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶסְתֵּר֙ אִם־עַל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב יִנָּתֵ֣ן גַּם־מָחָ֗ר לַיְּהוּדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשׁוּשָׁ֔ן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כְּדָ֣ת הַיּ֑וֹם וְאֵ֛ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת בְּנֵֽי־הָמָ֖ן יִתְל֥וּ עַל־הָעֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Esther, if on the king [it is] good, let it be given also tomorrow to the Jews who [are] in Susa to do according to [the] law of today; and [the] ten sons of Haman let them hang on the gallows.

en.L: And Esther said, "If it is good to the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Susa to act tomorrow also according to today's law, and let them hang the ten sons of Haman on the gallows."
en.B: Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa be allowed to act tomorrow too, as today's decree allows, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows."
en.R: Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa do again tomorrow what the law let them do today. And let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows."

es.L: Y dijo Ester: «Si al rey [le parece] bien, que se conceda también mañana a los judíos que [están] en Susa hacer conforme a la ley de hoy; y a los diez hijos de Amán, que los cuelguen en la horca».
es.B: Ester respondió: «Si al rey le parece bien, que se permita a los judíos de Susa actuar también mañana conforme al decreto de hoy, y que los diez hijos de Amán sean colgados en la horca».
es.R: Ester respondió: «Si al rey le parece bien, que los judíos de Susa hagan también mañana lo que la ley les permitió hacer hoy. Y que cuelguen en la horca a los diez hijos de Amán».

fr.L: Et Esther dit : « S’il [semble] bon au roi, qu’il soit accordé aux Juifs qui [sont] à Suse d’agir demain encore selon la loi d’aujourd’hui, et qu’on pende les dix fils de Haman à la potence. »
fr.B: Esther répondit : « S’il plaît au roi, qu’on permette aux Juifs de Suse d’agir demain encore selon le décret d’aujourd’hui, et que les dix fils de Haman soient pendus à la potence. »
fr.R: Esther a répondu : « Si le roi le veut bien, que les Juifs de Suse fassent encore demain ce que la loi leur a permis de faire aujourd’hui. Et qu’on pende à la potence les dix fils de Haman. »

sw.L: Esta akasema, "Ikiwa [ni] vema kwa mfalme, Wayahudi [walio] Shushani na waruhusiwe kesho pia kufanya kulingana na sheria ya leo; na wana kumi wa Hamani na watundikwe juu ya mti wa kunyongea."
sw.B: Esta akajibu, "Mfalme akipenda, Wayahudi wa Shushani na waruhusiwe kufanya kesho pia kama amri ya leo inavyoruhusu, na wana kumi wa Hamani watundikwe juu ya mti wa kunyongea."
sw.R: Esta akajibu, "Mfalme akipenda, Wayahudi wa Shushani na wafanye tena kesho kile ambacho sheria iliwaruhusu kufanya leo. Na wana kumi wa Hamani watundikwe juu ya mti wa kunyongea."

vi.L: Ê-xơ-tê thưa: "Nếu vua lấy làm tốt, xin cho người Do Thái [ở] tại Su-sơ ngày mai cũng được làm theo luật hôm nay; và xin cho treo mười con trai của Ha-man lên giá treo cổ."
vi.B: Ê-xơ-tê tâu: "Nếu đẹp lòng bệ hạ, xin cho người Do Thái ở Su-sơ ngày mai cũng được hành động theo chiếu chỉ hôm nay, và xin cho treo mười con trai của Ha-man lên giá treo cổ."
vi.R: Ê-xơ-tê thưa: "Nếu đức vua bằng lòng, xin cho người Do Thái ở Su-sơ ngày mai lại được làm những gì luật đã cho phép họ làm hôm nay. Và xin cho treo mười con trai của Ha-man lên giá treo cổ."

ko.L: 그러자 에스더가 말했다. "임금님께 좋으시면, 수산에 [있는] 유대인에게 내일도 오늘의 법령대로 행하도록 허락하시고, 하만의 열 아들을 교수대에 매달게 하십시오."
ko.B: 에스더가 대답했다. "임금님께서 좋게 여기시면, 수산에 있는 유대인이 내일도 오늘의 조서대로 행하도록 허락해 주시고, 하만의 열 아들을 교수대에 매달게 해 주십시오."
ko.R: 에스더가 대답했다. "임금님께서 괜찮으시다면, 수산에 있는 유대인이 오늘 법이 허락한 일을 내일도 하게 해 주십시오. 그리고 하만의 열 아들을 교수대에 매달게 해 주십시오."

decisions.choice: to act tomorrow according to today's law: the permission extended by one day in Susa
decisions.reason: The king's second decree allowed the Jews to defend themselves on the thirteenth of Adar only (8:11-12). Esther asks that the same permission hold in Susa for the fourteenth, which is why the Jews of Susa keep the feast a day later (9:18).

decisions.choice: hang the ten sons: display the bodies of men already dead
decisions.reason: The sons were already killed (9:10). Hanging the bodies in public was a mark of disgrace and a warning to others (1 Samuel 31:10; Deuteronomy 21:22-23). They are hanged on the gallows their father had prepared (5:14; 7:10).

decisions.choice: the gallows: a tall wooden pole
decisions.reason: The word means tree or wood. In Esther it is the pole Haman set up, fifty cubits high (5:14). Whether bodies were hanged from it or fixed on it as a stake is not certain.

decisions.choice: If it pleases the king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "if on the king [it is] good", the polite form of a request to a king (1:19; 5:4; 8:5). Literal keeps "good to the king".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְהֵֽעָשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן וַתִּנָּתֵ֥ן דָּ֖ת בְּשׁוּשָׁ֑ן וְאֵ֛ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת בְּנֵֽי־הָמָ֖ן תָּלֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to be done thus, and was given [the] law in Susa, and [the] ten sons of Haman they hanged.

en.L: And the king said for it to be done so; and a law was given out in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
en.B: So the king ordered that this be done. A decree was issued in Susa, and the ten sons of Haman were hanged.
en.R: So the king ordered it to be done. A law was announced in Susa, and Haman's ten sons were hanged.

es.L: Y dijo el rey que se hiciera así; y se dio la ley en Susa, y colgaron a los diez hijos de Amán.
es.B: Así que el rey ordenó que se hiciera esto. Se promulgó un decreto en Susa, y los diez hijos de Amán fueron colgados.
es.R: Entonces el rey ordenó que se hiciera así. Se anunció una ley en Susa, y colgaron a los diez hijos de Amán.

fr.L: Et le roi dit qu’on fasse ainsi ; et une loi fut donnée à Suse, et on pendit les dix fils de Haman.
fr.B: Le roi ordonna donc qu’on fasse ainsi. Un décret fut promulgué à Suse, et les dix fils de Haman furent pendus.
fr.R: Le roi a donc ordonné qu’on le fasse. Une loi a été annoncée à Suse, et on a pendu les dix fils de Haman.

sw.L: Mfalme akasema ifanyike hivyo; sheria ikatolewa katika Shushani, nao wakawatundika wana kumi wa Hamani.
sw.B: Basi mfalme akaagiza ifanyike hivyo. Amri ikatolewa katika Shushani, na wana kumi wa Hamani wakatundikwa.
sw.R: Basi mfalme akaamuru ifanyike hivyo. Sheria ikatangazwa katika Shushani, na wana kumi wa Hamani wakatundikwa.

vi.L: Vua truyền làm như vậy; luật được ban ra tại Su-sơ, và người ta treo mười con trai của Ha-man.
vi.B: Vậy vua truyền cho làm như thế. Một chiếu chỉ được ban hành tại Su-sơ, và mười con trai của Ha-man bị treo lên.
vi.R: Vậy vua ra lệnh làm như thế. Một đạo luật được loan báo tại Su-sơ, và mười con trai của Ha-man bị treo lên.

ko.L: 그러자 왕이 그렇게 하라고 말하였고, 수산에 법령이 내려졌으며, 사람들이 하만의 열 아들을 매달았다.
ko.B: 그리하여 왕은 그렇게 하라고 명령했다. 수산에 조서가 내려졌고, 하만의 열 아들이 매달렸다.
ko.R: 그래서 왕은 그렇게 하라고 명령했다. 수산에 법이 발표되었고, 하만의 열 아들이 매달렸다.

decisions.choice: they hanged: an impersonal plural, "were hanged"
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; it means the order was carried out by those responsible, as also in 9:25.

decisions.choice: a law was given: a decree was published
decisions.reason: To give a law is to issue it publicly, as in 3:14-15 and 8:13-14.

source.text: וַיִּֽקָּהֲל֞וּ הַיְּהוּדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן גַּ֠ם בְּי֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר וַיַּֽהַרְג֣וּ בְשׁוּשָׁ֔ן שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־יָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And assembled the Jews who [were] in Susa also on [the] fourteenth day of [the] month Adar, and they killed in Susa three hundred men; and on the plunder not they stretched out their hand.

en.L: And the Jews who were in Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and they killed in Susa 300 men; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
en.B: The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of the month Adar and killed 300 men in Susa. But they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
en.R: The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of Adar, and they killed 300 men in the city. But they did not take anything for themselves.

es.L: Y se reunieron los judíos que [estaban] en Susa también el día catorce del mes de Adar, y mataron en Susa a 300 hombres; pero en el botín no echaron mano.
es.B: Los judíos de Susa se reunieron de nuevo el día catorce del mes de Adar y mataron a 300 hombres en Susa. Pero no tocaron el botín.
es.R: Los judíos de Susa se reunieron otra vez el día catorce de Adar y mataron a 300 hombres en la ciudad. Pero no se quedaron con nada.

fr.L: Et les Juifs qui [étaient] à Suse se rassemblèrent aussi le quatorzième jour du mois d’Adar, et ils tuèrent à Suse 300 hommes ; mais sur le butin ils ne portèrent pas la main.
fr.B: Les Juifs de Suse se rassemblèrent encore le quatorzième jour du mois d’Adar et tuèrent 300 hommes à Suse. Mais ils ne touchèrent pas au butin.
fr.R: Les Juifs de Suse se sont de nouveau rassemblés le quatorzième jour d’Adar, et ils ont tué 300 hommes dans la ville. Mais ils n’ont rien pris pour eux.

sw.L: Wayahudi [waliokuwa] Shushani wakakusanyika pia siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa Adari, wakaua watu 300 katika Shushani; lakini hawakunyosha mkono wao juu ya nyara.
sw.B: Wayahudi wa Shushani walikusanyika tena siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa Adari, wakaua watu 300 katika Shushani. Lakini hawakugusa nyara.
sw.R: Wayahudi wa Shushani walikusanyika tena siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa Adari, wakaua watu 300 katika mji. Lakini hawakujichukulia chochote.

vi.L: Người Do Thái [ở] tại Su-sơ cũng tụ họp vào ngày mười bốn tháng A-đa, và họ giết 300 người tại Su-sơ; nhưng họ không tra tay vào của cướp.
vi.B: Người Do Thái ở Su-sơ lại tụ họp vào ngày mười bốn tháng A-đa và giết 300 người tại Su-sơ. Nhưng họ không đụng đến của cướp.
vi.R: Người Do Thái ở Su-sơ lại tụ họp vào ngày mười bốn tháng A-đa, và giết 300 người trong thành. Nhưng họ không lấy gì cho mình.

ko.L: 그리고 수산에 [있는] 유대인이 아달 월 십사일에도 모여 수산에서 300명을 죽였다. 그러나 노략물에는 손을 대지 않았다.
ko.B: 수산에 있는 유대인은 아달 월 십사일에 다시 모여 수산에서 300명을 죽였다. 그러나 노략물에는 손을 대지 않았다.
ko.R: 수산에 있는 유대인은 아달 월 십사일에 다시 모여 성 안에서 300명을 죽였다. 그러나 그들은 아무것도 자기 것으로 가지지 않았다.

decisions.choice: also on the fourteenth: the second day granted at Esther's request
decisions.reason: This carries out the extra day of verse 13. The figure of 300 is for the city of Susa beyond the citadel count of verse 6.

decisions.choice: they did not lay their hand on the plunder
decisions.reason: The second of three such statements (9:10, 16); see the decision at 9:10.

source.text: וּשְׁאָ֣ר הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ בִּמְדִינ֨וֹת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ נִקְהֲל֣וּ׀וְעָמֹ֣ד עַל־נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְנ֨וֹחַ֙ מֵאֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָרֹג֙ בְּשֹׂ֣נְאֵיהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָֽׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־יָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of the Jews who [were] in [the] provinces of the king assembled and stood for their life, and rested from their enemies, and killed among [those] hating them five and seventy thousand; and on the plunder not they stretched out their hand.

en.L: And the rest of the Jews who were in the king's provinces assembled and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and killed 75,000 of those who hated them; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
en.B: Meanwhile the rest of the Jews in the king's provinces gathered to defend their lives, and they had rest from their enemies. They killed 75,000 of those who hated them, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
en.R: At the same time, the other Jews in the king's provinces gathered to protect themselves, and they were set free from their enemies. They killed 75,000 of the people who hated them. But they did not take anything for themselves.

es.L: Y el resto de los judíos que [estaban] en las provincias del rey se reunieron y defendieron su vida, y tuvieron reposo de sus enemigos, y mataron de los que los aborrecían a 75 000; pero en el botín no echaron mano.
es.B: Mientras tanto, el resto de los judíos de las provincias del rey se reunieron para defender su vida, y tuvieron reposo de sus enemigos. Mataron a 75 000 de los que los odiaban, pero no tocaron el botín.
es.R: Al mismo tiempo, los otros judíos de las provincias del rey se reunieron para protegerse, y quedaron libres de sus enemigos. Mataron a 75 000 de los que los odiaban. Pero no se quedaron con nada.

fr.L: Et le reste des Juifs qui [étaient] dans les provinces du roi se rassemblèrent et défendirent leur vie, et ils eurent du repos face à leurs ennemis, et ils tuèrent 75 000 de ceux qui les haïssaient ; mais sur le butin ils ne portèrent pas la main.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, les autres Juifs des provinces du roi se rassemblèrent pour défendre leur vie, et ils trouvèrent le repos face à leurs ennemis. Ils tuèrent 75 000 de ceux qui les haïssaient, mais ils ne touchèrent pas au butin.
fr.R: Au même moment, les autres Juifs des provinces du roi se sont rassemblés pour se défendre, et ils ont été délivrés de leurs ennemis. Ils ont tué 75 000 de ceux qui les haïssaient. Mais ils n’ont rien pris pour eux.

sw.L: Na Wayahudi wengine [waliokuwa] katika majimbo ya mfalme wakakusanyika, wakasimama kwa ajili ya uhai wao, wakapata raha kutoka kwa adui zao, wakaua watu 75,000 wa wale waliowachukia; lakini hawakunyosha mkono wao juu ya nyara.
sw.B: Wakati huo huo Wayahudi wengine katika majimbo ya mfalme walikusanyika kuyatetea maisha yao, wakapata raha kutoka kwa adui zao. Waliua watu 75,000 wa wale waliowachukia, lakini hawakugusa nyara.
sw.R: Wakati huo huo, Wayahudi wengine katika majimbo ya mfalme walikusanyika kujilinda, wakawekwa huru kutoka kwa adui zao. Waliua watu 75,000 wa wale waliowachukia. Lakini hawakujichukulia chochote.

vi.L: Những người Do Thái còn lại [ở] trong các tỉnh của vua cũng tụ họp và đứng lên bảo vệ mạng sống mình, được yên nghỉ khỏi kẻ thù, và giết 75.000 người trong số những kẻ ghét mình; nhưng họ không tra tay vào của cướp.
vi.B: Trong khi đó, những người Do Thái khác trong các tỉnh của vua tụ họp lại để bảo vệ mạng sống mình, và được yên ổn khỏi kẻ thù. Họ giết 75.000 người trong số những kẻ ghét mình, nhưng không đụng đến của cướp.
vi.R: Cùng lúc ấy, những người Do Thái khác trong các tỉnh của vua tụ họp lại để tự vệ, và được thoát khỏi kẻ thù. Họ giết 75.000 người trong số những kẻ ghét mình. Nhưng họ không lấy gì cho mình.

ko.L: 그리고 왕의 지방들에 [있는] 나머지 유대인도 모여 자기 목숨을 지키고, 원수들에게서 벗어나 쉼을 얻었으며, 자기들을 미워하는 자들 가운데 75,000명을 죽였다. 그러나 노략물에는 손을 대지 않았다.
ko.B: 한편 왕의 지방들에 있는 나머지 유대인도 모여서 자기 목숨을 지키고, 원수들에게서 벗어나 평안을 얻었다. 그들은 자기들을 미워하는 자들 가운데 75,000명을 죽였으나, 노략물에는 손을 대지 않았다.
ko.R: 같은 때에 왕의 지방들에 사는 다른 유대인도 모여서 자신들을 지켰고, 원수들에게서 풀려났다. 그들은 자기들을 미워하는 사람 75,000명을 죽였다. 그러나 아무것도 자기 것으로 가지지 않았다.

decisions.choice: stood for their life: defended themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the wording of the king's second decree (8:11), which allowed the Jews to stand up for their lives.

decisions.choice: rested from their enemies: were relieved of them, had peace from them
decisions.reason: Rest here is safety from attack, as the land had rest from enemies under the judges and David (Joshua 21:44; 2 Samuel 7:1). The same rest is what the feast remembers (9:17-18, 22).

decisions.choice: seventy-five thousand (the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has 75,000. The old Greek translation of Esther has 15,000. The Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: they were set free from their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable puts "rested from" in plain words; the sense is relief from attack (m2).

source.text: בְּיוֹם־שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֑ר וְנ֗וֹחַ בְּאַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וְעָשֹׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ י֖וֹם מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה וְשִׂמְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] thirteenth day of [the] month Adar; and resting on [the] fourteenth in it, and making it a day of feasting and joy.

en.L: [This was] on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and they rested on its fourteenth and made it a day of feasting and joy.
en.B: This was on the thirteenth day of the month Adar. On the fourteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.
en.R: This happened on the thirteenth day of Adar. On the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.

es.L: [Esto fue] el día trece del mes de Adar; y reposaron el día catorce del mismo, y lo hicieron día de banquete y de alegría.
es.B: Esto fue el día trece del mes de Adar. El día catorce reposaron y lo hicieron día de banquete y de alegría.
es.R: Esto sucedió el día trece de Adar. El día catorce descansaron y lo hicieron un día de banquete y de alegría.

fr.L: [Ce fut] le treizième jour du mois d’Adar ; et ils se reposèrent le quatorzième du mois, et ils en firent un jour de festin et de joie.
fr.B: Cela se passa le treizième jour du mois d’Adar. Le quatorzième, ils se reposèrent et en firent un jour de festin et de joie.
fr.R: Cela s’est passé le treizième jour d’Adar. Le quatorzième jour, ils se sont reposés et ils en ont fait un jour de festin et de joie.

sw.L: [Hayo yalikuwa] siku ya kumi na tatu ya mwezi wa Adari; wakapumzika siku yake ya kumi na nne, wakaifanya kuwa siku ya karamu na furaha.
sw.B: Hayo yalikuwa siku ya kumi na tatu ya mwezi wa Adari. Siku ya kumi na nne walipumzika, wakaifanya kuwa siku ya karamu na furaha.
sw.R: Hayo yalitukia siku ya kumi na tatu ya mwezi wa Adari. Siku ya kumi na nne walipumzika, wakaifanya kuwa siku ya karamu na furaha.

vi.L: [Việc ấy xảy ra] vào ngày mười ba tháng A-đa; và họ nghỉ ngơi vào ngày mười bốn của tháng ấy, và lấy ngày đó làm ngày tiệc tùng và vui mừng.
vi.B: Việc ấy xảy ra vào ngày mười ba tháng A-đa. Đến ngày mười bốn, họ nghỉ ngơi và lấy ngày đó làm ngày tiệc tùng vui mừng.
vi.R: Việc ấy xảy ra vào ngày mười ba tháng A-đa. Đến ngày mười bốn họ nghỉ ngơi, và biến ngày đó thành ngày tiệc tùng vui mừng.

ko.L: [그것은] 아달 월 십삼일이었다. 그리고 그달 십사일에 쉬면서 그날을 잔치와 기쁨의 날로 삼았다.
ko.B: 그것은 아달 월 십삼일의 일이었다. 십사일에 그들은 쉬면서 그날을 잔치하며 기뻐하는 날로 삼았다.
ko.R: 이 일은 아달 월 십삼일에 있었다. 십사일에 그들은 쉬었고, 그날을 잔치를 벌이며 기뻐하는 날로 삼았다.

decisions.choice: On the thirteenth: dating the fighting in the provinces of verse 16
decisions.reason: The verse begins with a bare date. It ties the fighting of verse 16 to the thirteenth, and the rest and feast to the next day, in contrast with Susa (verse 18).

decisions.choice: a day of feasting and joy
decisions.reason: The word for feast is the one used for drinking banquets throughout the book: the king's feasts (1:3, 5) and Esther's (5:4; 7:2). The book that began with the king's feasting ends with the Jews' own.

decisions.choice: [This was] (L); This was (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew date stands with no verb; English supplies one.

source.text: וְהַיְּהוּדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן נִקְהֲלוּ֙ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וּבְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר בּ֑וֹ וְנ֗וֹחַ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וְעָשֹׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ י֖וֹם מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה וְשִׂמְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the Jews who [were] in Susa assembled on [the] thirteenth in it and on [the] fourteenth in it, and resting on [the] fifteenth in it, and making it a day of feasting and joy.

en.L: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled on its thirteenth and on its fourteenth, and they rested on its fifteenth and made it a day of feasting and joy.
en.B: But the Jews in Susa had gathered on both the thirteenth and the fourteenth, so they rested on the fifteenth and made it a day of feasting and joy.
en.R: But the Jews in Susa had gathered to fight on both the thirteenth and the fourteenth. So they rested on the fifteenth and made that their day of feasting and joy.

es.L: Pero los judíos que [estaban] en Susa se reunieron el día trece y el día catorce del mismo, y reposaron el día quince del mismo, y lo hicieron día de banquete y de alegría.
es.B: Pero los judíos de Susa se habían reunido tanto el día trece como el catorce, así que reposaron el día quince y lo hicieron día de banquete y de alegría.
es.R: Pero los judíos de Susa se habían reunido para luchar el día trece y también el catorce. Por eso descansaron el día quince e hicieron de ese día su día de banquete y de alegría.

fr.L: Mais les Juifs qui [étaient] à Suse se rassemblèrent le treizième et le quatorzième du mois, et ils se reposèrent le quinzième du mois, et ils en firent un jour de festin et de joie.
fr.B: Mais les Juifs de Suse s’étaient rassemblés le treizième et le quatorzième jour ; ils se reposèrent donc le quinzième et en firent un jour de festin et de joie.
fr.R: Mais les Juifs de Suse s’étaient rassemblés pour combattre le treizième et le quatorzième jour. Ils se sont donc reposés le quinzième, et ils en ont fait leur jour de festin et de joie.

sw.L: Lakini Wayahudi [waliokuwa] Shushani walikusanyika siku yake ya kumi na tatu na siku yake ya kumi na nne, wakapumzika siku yake ya kumi na tano, wakaifanya kuwa siku ya karamu na furaha.
sw.B: Lakini Wayahudi wa Shushani walikuwa wamekusanyika siku ya kumi na tatu na siku ya kumi na nne, kwa hiyo walipumzika siku ya kumi na tano, wakaifanya kuwa siku ya karamu na furaha.
sw.R: Lakini Wayahudi wa Shushani walikuwa wamekusanyika kupigana siku ya kumi na tatu na pia siku ya kumi na nne. Kwa hiyo walipumzika siku ya kumi na tano, wakaifanya siku hiyo kuwa siku yao ya karamu na furaha.

vi.L: Nhưng người Do Thái [ở] tại Su-sơ đã tụ họp vào ngày mười ba và ngày mười bốn của tháng ấy, và họ nghỉ ngơi vào ngày mười lăm của tháng ấy, và lấy ngày đó làm ngày tiệc tùng và vui mừng.
vi.B: Nhưng người Do Thái ở Su-sơ đã tụ họp cả ngày mười ba lẫn ngày mười bốn, nên họ nghỉ ngơi vào ngày mười lăm và lấy ngày đó làm ngày tiệc tùng vui mừng.
vi.R: Nhưng người Do Thái ở Su-sơ đã tụ họp để chiến đấu cả ngày mười ba lẫn ngày mười bốn. Vì thế họ nghỉ ngơi vào ngày mười lăm, và lấy ngày ấy làm ngày tiệc tùng vui mừng của mình.

ko.L: 그러나 수산에 [있는] 유대인은 그달 십삼일과 그달 십사일에 모였고, 그달 십오일에 쉬면서 그날을 잔치와 기쁨의 날로 삼았다.
ko.B: 그러나 수산에 있는 유대인은 십삼일과 십사일 이틀 동안 모였으므로, 십오일에 쉬면서 그날을 잔치하며 기뻐하는 날로 삼았다.
ko.R: 그러나 수산에 있는 유대인은 십삼일과 십사일에 모여서 싸웠다. 그래서 그들은 십오일에 쉬었고, 그날을 잔치를 벌이며 기뻐하는 날로 삼았다.

decisions.choice: Susa's feast on the fifteenth
decisions.reason: Because the fighting in Susa lasted two days (9:13-15), the Jews there rested a day later. This is the origin of the two dates in verses 19 and 21; Jewish practice still keeps Purim on the fifteenth in walled cities and on the fourteenth elsewhere.

decisions.choice: gathered to fight
decisions.reason: Readable says why they gathered, as verses 2 and 15 make clear.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֞ן הַיְּהוּדִ֣ים הַפְּרָזִ֗ים הַיֹּשְׁבִים֮ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַפְּרָזוֹת֒ עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֠ת י֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר שִׂמְחָ֥ה וּמִשְׁתֶּ֖ה וְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב וּמִשְׁל֥וֹחַ מָנ֖וֹת אִ֥ישׁ לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Therefore the Jews, the villagers who dwell in [the] cities of the open country, [are] making [the] fourteenth day of [the] month Adar joy and feasting and a good day, and sending portions each to his neighbor.

en.L: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar [a day of] joy and feasting and a good day, and of sending portions {{gender:each one to their neighbor|each man to his neighbor}}.
en.B: That is why the Jews of the villages, who live in unwalled towns, keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar as a day of joy and feasting, a holiday, when they send gifts of food to one another.
en.R: That is why Jews who live in villages and towns without walls celebrate on the fourteenth day of Adar. It is a happy holiday with feasting, and people send gifts of food to each other.

es.L: Por eso los judíos de las aldeas, que habitan en las ciudades sin muros, hacen del día catorce del mes de Adar [día de] alegría y de banquete y día bueno, y de enviar porciones {{gender:cada persona a su prójimo|cada hombre a su prójimo}}.
es.B: Por eso los judíos de las aldeas, que viven en ciudades sin muros, celebran el día catorce del mes de Adar como día de alegría y de banquete, un día de fiesta, en el que se envían regalos de comida unos a otros.
es.R: Por eso los judíos que viven en aldeas y pueblos sin muros celebran el día catorce de Adar. Es un día feliz de fiesta y banquetes, y la gente se envía regalos de comida unos a otros.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi les Juifs des villages, qui habitent dans les villes sans murailles, font du quatorzième jour du mois d’Adar [un jour de] joie et de festin et un jour de fête, et d’envoi de portions, {{gender:chaque personne|chaque homme}} à son prochain.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi les Juifs des villages, qui habitent dans des villes sans murailles, célèbrent le quatorzième jour du mois d’Adar comme un jour de joie et de festin, un jour de fête où l’on s’envoie des parts de nourriture les uns aux autres.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi les Juifs qui vivent dans les villages et les villes sans murailles font la fête le quatorzième jour d’Adar. C’est un jour heureux, avec des festins, et les gens s’envoient de la nourriture en cadeau les uns aux autres.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo Wayahudi wa vijijini, wanaoishi katika miji isiyo na kuta, huifanya siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa Adari kuwa [siku ya] furaha na karamu na siku njema, na ya kupelekeana sehemu za chakula kila mtu kwa jirani yake.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu Wayahudi wa vijijini, wanaoishi katika miji isiyo na kuta, huiadhimisha siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa Adari kuwa siku ya furaha na karamu, sikukuu, ambayo hupelekeana zawadi za chakula.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu Wayahudi wanaoishi vijijini na katika miji isiyo na kuta husherehekea siku ya kumi na nne ya mwezi wa Adari. Ni sikukuu ya furaha yenye karamu, na watu hupelekeana zawadi za chakula.

vi.L: Vì thế, người Do Thái ở thôn quê, là những người sống trong các thành không có tường bao, lấy ngày mười bốn tháng A-đa làm [ngày] vui mừng, tiệc tùng và ngày lành, và gửi phần ăn cho nhau, người này cho người lân cận mình.
vi.B: Vì thế, người Do Thái ở thôn quê, sống trong các thành không có tường bao, giữ ngày mười bốn tháng A-đa làm ngày vui mừng và tiệc tùng, một ngày lễ, và gửi quà thức ăn cho nhau.
vi.R: Vì thế, người Do Thái sống ở các làng và thị trấn không có tường thành ăn mừng vào ngày mười bốn tháng A-đa. Đó là một ngày lễ vui vẻ với tiệc tùng, và người ta gửi quà thức ăn cho nhau.

ko.L: 그러므로 성벽 없는 성읍들에 사는 시골의 유대인은 아달 월 십사일을 기쁨과 잔치와 좋은 날로 삼고, 각 사람이 자기 이웃에게 음식을 나누어 보낸다.
ko.B: 그래서 성벽 없는 성읍에 사는 시골의 유대인은 아달 월 십사일을 기뻐하며 잔치하는 날, 곧 명절로 지키고, 서로 음식을 나누어 보낸다.
ko.R: 그래서 성벽이 없는 마을과 성읍에 사는 유대인은 아달 월 십사일에 축제를 연다. 그날은 잔치를 벌이는 즐거운 명절이고, 사람들은 서로 음식을 선물로 보낸다.

decisions.choice: villagers in the towns of the open country: Jews in unwalled settlements
decisions.reason: The words describe open country and towns without walls (Deuteronomy 3:5; Ezekiel 38:11), in contrast with fortified Susa. The Hebrew has two spellings of the first word in the written and the read text; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a good day: a festival, a holiday
decisions.reason: A good day is a day of celebration (8:17; 1 Samuel 25:8).

decisions.choice: sending portions: giving gifts of food
decisions.reason: Portions are shares of food from a feast, sent to others (Nehemiah 8:10, 12). The present tense ("make") speaks from the writer's own time, when the custom was already kept.

decisions.choice: each one to their neighbor / each man to his neighbor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom means one another, men and women alike, so Literal uses the gender setting; Balanced and Readable say "one another".

decisions.choice: {{gender:cada persona a su prójimo|cada hombre a su prójimo}}
decisions.reason: As in the English Literal: the Hebrew 'each man' means men and women alike; Balanced and Readable say «unos a otros».

decisions.choice: {{gender:chaque personne|chaque homme}} à son prochain
decisions.reason: As in the English Literal: the Hebrew 'each man' means men and women alike; the span sits on the noun, as the French rule asks. Balanced and Readable say « les uns aux autres ».

source.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מָרְדֳּכַ֔י אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סְפָרִ֜ים אֶל־כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּכָל־מְדִינוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ הַקְּרוֹבִ֖ים וְהָרְחוֹקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And wrote Mordecai the words the these, and sent letters to all the Jews who [were] in all [the] provinces of the king Ahasuerus, the near and the far,

en.L: And Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far,
en.B: Mordecai recorded these events, and he sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far,
en.R: Mordecai wrote down what had happened. He sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far.

decisions.choice: wrote these things: recorded the events just told
alternatives: wrote these words (the letter that follows)
decisions.reason: The words can mean these events or these words. Most likely Mordecai wrote down what had happened as the ground for the feast; it may also mean the instructions that follow in his letters.

decisions.choice: a full stop at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 21. Readable ends it here and begins verse 21 with "He told them".

source.text: לְקַיֵּם֮ עֲלֵיהֶם֒ לִהְי֣וֹת עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֠ת י֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר וְאֵ֛ת יוֹם־חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר בּ֑וֹ בְּכָל־שָׁנָ֖ה וְשָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: to establish on them to be observing [the] fourteenth day of [the] month Adar and [the] fifteenth day in it, in every year and year,

en.L: to establish for them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar and its fifteenth day, every year,
en.B: to require them to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar every year,
en.R: He told them to celebrate the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar every year.

decisions.choice: to establish on them: to make it binding on them
decisions.reason: The verb means to set up or confirm, and with "on them" to make something a fixed duty. It is the key word of the chapter's ending (9:27, 29, 31, 32).

decisions.choice: the fourteenth and the fifteenth: both days of the feast
alternatives: every Jew to keep both days
decisions.reason: The letter names both days. Read with verses 18-19, it fixes the fourteenth for the villages and the fifteenth for Susa; it may also mean that both days were to be kept by all.

decisions.choice: He told them
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence here (see 9:20) and supplies a subject and verb.

source.text: כַּיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־נָ֨חוּ בָהֶ֤ם הַיְּהוּדִים֙ מֵא֣וֹיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וְהַחֹ֗דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר֩ נֶהְפַּ֨ךְ לָהֶ֤ם מִיָּגוֹן֙ לְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּמֵאֵ֖בֶל לְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אוֹתָ֗ם יְמֵי֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה וְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּמִשְׁל֤וֹחַ מָנוֹת֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּמַתָּנ֖וֹת לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: as [the] days on which had rest the Jews from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day; to make them days of feasting and joy and sending portions each to his neighbor and gifts to the poor.

en.L: as the days on which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow into joy and from mourning into a good day; to make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions {{gender:each one to their neighbor|each man to his neighbor}}, and gifts to the poor.
en.B: as the days when the Jews got rest from their enemies, and as the month that was turned for them from grief into joy and from mourning into a holiday. They were to make them days of feasting and joy, of sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor.
en.R: These were the days when the Jews were set free from their enemies. That month their sadness turned into joy, and their mourning into a holiday. So they were to celebrate with feasts and joy, send gifts of food to each other, and give gifts to poor people.

decisions.choice: turned from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the great reversal in 9:1. The month of Adar had been the month of fasting and sackcloth when Haman's decree came (4:1-3); now it becomes a month of celebration.

decisions.choice: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Along with feasting and gifts of food to friends, the feast includes care for the poor, a custom of Purim still kept.

decisions.choice: a new sentence for "to make them days of feasting"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs from verse 20 through this verse. Balanced and Readable break it so it can be followed.

source.text: וְקִבֵּל֙ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הֵחֵ֖לּוּ לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־כָּתַ֥ב מָרְדֳּכַ֖י אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And accepted the Jews what they had begun to do, and what had written Mordecai to them.

en.L: And the Jews accepted what they had begun to do, and what Mordecai had written to them.
en.B: So the Jews made a custom of what they had begun to do, and of what Mordecai had written to them.
en.R: So the Jews agreed to keep on doing what they had started to do, as Mordecai had written to them.

decisions.choice: accepted: took on as a binding custom
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or take upon oneself. The feast began with what the Jews did of their own accord (9:17-19), and Mordecai's letter made it a fixed practice; the people accepted both. The same verb returns in 9:27.

decisions.choice: made a custom of
decisions.reason: "Accepted" alone could sound like mere agreement; Balanced says what the Jews took on.

source.text: כִּי֩ הָמָ֨ן בֶּֽן־הַמְּדָ֜תָא הָֽאֲגָגִ֗י צֹרֵר֙ כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים חָשַׁ֥ב עַל־הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים לְאַבְּדָ֑ם וְהִפִּ֥יל פּוּר֙ ה֣וּא הַגּוֹרָ֔ל לְהֻמָּ֖ם וּֽלְאַבְּדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, [the] harasser of all the Jews, had planned against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that [is] the lot, to throw them into confusion and to destroy them.

en.L: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to crush them and to destroy them.
en.B: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them. He had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to crush and destroy them.
en.R: This was because Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had made plans to destroy them. He had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to choose the day to crush them and destroy them.

decisions.choice: Pur, that is, the lot
decisions.reason: Pur is a foreign word, from the Akkadian language of Babylon, for a lot used to decide something by chance. The writer explains it with the ordinary Hebrew word for lot, as in 3:7, where Haman had the lot cast to choose the month and day of the killing. The feast takes its name from it (verse 26).

decisions.choice: to throw them into confusion: to crush them
decisions.reason: The verb means to rout or throw into panic, a word used for the LORD routing an enemy army (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10). It sounds like Haman's own name, which may be a play on words; the text does not point it out.

decisions.choice: the Agagite
decisions.reason: See the decision at 3:1 on the link with Agag king of Amalek. Here at the end, the whole of Haman's plot is summed up in one sentence.

decisions.choice: to choose the day
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lot was for, as 3:7 tells; the Hebrew here leaves it implied.

source.text: וּבְבֹאָהּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ אָמַ֣ר עִם־הַסֵּ֔פֶר יָשׁ֞וּב מַחֲשַׁבְתּ֧וֹ הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־חָשַׁ֥ב עַל־הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וְתָל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו עַל־הָעֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And when she came before the king, he said with the letter, let return his plan the evil which he had planned against the Jews on his head; and they hanged him and his sons on the gallows.

en.L: But when she came before the king, he said by letter that his evil plan which he had plotted against the Jews should return on his own head, and they hanged him and his sons on the gallows.
en.B: But when Esther came before the king, he gave orders in writing that the evil plan Haman had plotted against the Jews should fall back on his own head, and Haman and his sons were hanged on the gallows.
en.R: But when Esther went to the king, the king gave orders in writing. The evil plan that Haman had made against the Jews would happen to Haman himself instead. So Haman and his sons were hanged on the gallows.

decisions.choice: when she came: when Esther came before the king
alternatives: when the matter came before the king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "when she (or it) came before the king". It most likely means Esther, who went to the king (5:1-2; 8:3); it can also mean "when the matter came before the king".

decisions.choice: return on his head: come back on the one who planned it
decisions.reason: To have one's evil return on one's own head is to suffer the harm one meant for others (1 Kings 2:44; Psalm 7:17). This is the reversal of 9:1 in Haman's own life.

decisions.choice: he said with the letter: he gave written orders
decisions.reason: This is a short summary of chapters 7-8. Haman's hanging was ordered by word of mouth (7:9), and the letters reversing his plot were sent afterward (8:8-10); the verse puts the king's orders together.

decisions.choice: Esther; Haman
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people the Hebrew pronouns point to, following m1.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֡ן קָֽרְאוּ֩ לַיָּמִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה פוּרִים֙ עַל־שֵׁ֣ם הַפּ֔וּר עַל־כֵּ֕ן עַל־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הָאִגֶּ֣רֶת הַזֹּ֑את וּמָֽה־רָא֣וּ עַל־כָּ֔כָה וּמָ֥ה הִגִּ֖יעַ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore they called the days the these Purim, on [the] name of the Pur; therefore, because of all [the] words of the letter the this, and what they had seen concerning this, and what had come to them,

en.L: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and of what they had seen concerning this, and what had come upon them,
en.B: That is why these days are called Purim, from the word Pur. And so, because of everything written in this letter, and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,
en.R: That is why these days are called Purim, from the word Pur, which means "lot". Because of everything in Mordecai's letter, and because of all that they had seen and all that had happened to them,

decisions.choice: Purim: the plural of Pur, "lots"
decisions.reason: The feast is named after the lot Haman cast to fix the day for destroying the Jews (3:7; 9:24). The day chosen for their death became the day of their rescue.

decisions.choice: this letter: Mordecai's letter of verse 20
decisions.reason: The letter is the one Mordecai sent to all the provinces (9:20-22).

decisions.choice: what they had seen concerning this: what they had lived through
decisions.reason: The Jews keep the feast both because of the letter and because of their own experience of the danger and the rescue.

decisions.choice: Mordecai's letter; which means "lot"
decisions.reason: Readable names whose letter it was and repeats the meaning of Pur from 9:24.

source.text: קִיְּמ֣וּ וְקִבְּל֣וּהַיְּהוּדִים֩׀עֲלֵיהֶ֨ם׀וְעַל־זַרְעָ֜ם וְעַ֨ל כָּל־הַנִּלְוִ֤ים עֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲב֔וֹר לִהְי֣וֹת עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י הַיָּמִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה כִּכְתָבָ֖ם וְכִזְמַנָּ֑ם בְּכָל־שָׁנָ֖ה וְשָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: established and accepted the Jews on themselves and on their offspring and on all [those] joining themselves to them, and it will not pass away, to be observing [the] two the days the these according to their writing and according to their appointed time in every year and year.

en.L: the Jews established and took upon themselves and upon their descendants and upon all who joined themselves to them, so that it should not pass away, to keep these two days as it was written about them and at their appointed time, every year.
en.B: the Jews made it a binding custom for themselves, for their descendants and for all who joined them, that without fail they would keep these two days, as it was written and at the appointed time every year.
en.R: the Jews made it a rule for themselves, for their descendants and for everyone who joined them. They would never stop celebrating these two days every year in the way that was written and at the right time.

decisions.choice: all who joined themselves to them: people of other nations who joined the Jews
decisions.reason: The words describe outsiders who attached themselves to the Jewish people and its God, like the many who became Jews in 8:17 (see also Isaiah 56:3, 6).

decisions.choice: established and accepted: made a binding rule and took it on
decisions.reason: The two verbs from verses 21 and 23 come together: what was set up for the Jews they now take upon themselves. The written Hebrew text has the second verb in the singular, the text read aloud in the plural; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: according to their writing and their time: as written, on the set dates
decisions.reason: The days are to be kept as the letters described them (9:20-22) and on their fixed dates, the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar.

decisions.choice: without fail; never stop
decisions.reason: "It will not pass away" means the practice must never lapse; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: וְהַיָּמִ֣ים הָ֠אֵלֶּה נִזְכָּרִ֨ים וְנַעֲשִׂ֜ים בְּכָל־דּ֣וֹר וָד֗וֹר מִשְׁפָּחָה֙ וּמִשְׁפָּחָ֔ה מְדִינָ֥ה וּמְדִינָ֖ה וְעִ֣יר וָעִ֑יר וִימֵ֞י הַפּוּרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה לֹ֤א יַֽעַבְרוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְזִכְרָ֖ם לֹא־יָס֥וּף מִזַּרְעָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the days the these [are] remembered and done in every generation and generation, clan and clan, province and province, and city and city; and [the] days of the Purim the these will not pass away from among the Jews, and their remembrance will not come to an end from their offspring.

en.L: And these days are to be remembered and kept in every generation, every clan, every province and every city; and these days of Purim shall not pass away from among the Jews, and the memory of them shall not come to an end among their descendants.
en.B: These days are to be remembered and kept in every generation, by every clan, in every province and in every city. These days of Purim must never disappear from among the Jews, and the memory of them must never fade among their descendants.
en.R: These days must be remembered and celebrated in every generation, by every family, in every province and in every city. The Jews must never stop keeping these days of Purim, and their descendants must always remember them.

decisions.choice: remembered and done: are to be remembered and kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses participles, which here describe a lasting rule for the future.

decisions.choice: generation and generation, clan and clan: every generation, every clan
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun is the Hebrew way of saying "every"; the list moves from time (generations) to people (clans) to places (provinces and cities).

decisions.choice: their remembrance: the memory of these days
decisions.reason: The feast exists so that the rescue is remembered. The verb for coming to an end means to cease or be finished.

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for clan, as elsewhere.

source.text: וַ֠תִּכְתֹּב אֶסְתֵּ֨ר הַמַּלְכָּ֧ה בַת־אֲבִיחַ֛יִל וּמָרְדֳּכַ֥י הַיְּהוּדִ֖י אֶת־כָּל־תֹּ֑קֶף לְקַיֵּ֗ם אֵ֣ת אִגֶּ֧רֶת הַפּוּרִ֛ים הַזֹּ֖את הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And wrote Esther the queen, [the] daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, with all authority, to confirm the letter of the Purim the this, the second.

en.L: And Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
en.B: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim.
en.R: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote a second letter about Purim. They used all their authority to make it official.

decisions.choice: she wrote: Esther as the main writer
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine and singular, with Esther named first and Mordecai added after. The queen now writes with her own authority, as Mordecai had done before (9:20). She is named with her father, Abihail (2:15), as at her first appearance before the king.

decisions.choice: this second letter of Purim
alternatives: to confirm (a second time) the letter of Purim
decisions.reason: This most likely means a second letter, after Mordecai's (9:20), written to confirm the feast. It can also be read as confirming the earlier letter a second time.

decisions.choice: all authority: full power
decisions.reason: The word means power or strength; it is used of the king's might in 10:2.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סְפָרִ֜ים אֶל־כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֶל־שֶׁ֨בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּמֵאָה֙ מְדִינָ֔ה מַלְכ֖וּת אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ דִּבְרֵ֥י שָׁל֖וֹם וֶאֱמֶֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent letters to all the Jews, to [the] seven and twenty and hundred province[s], [the] kingdom of Ahasuerus, words of peace and truth,

en.L: And he sent letters to all the Jews, to the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, words of peace and truth,
en.B: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,
en.R: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus. They were words of peace and truth,

decisions.choice: he sent: most likely Mordecai
decisions.reason: The verb is masculine singular. It most likely means Mordecai, named in verse 29; it may also be impersonal, "letters were sent".

decisions.choice: words of peace and truth: words of goodwill and assurance
decisions.reason: Peace is well-being and good relations; truth is faithfulness, words that can be relied on. The pair also appears in Zechariah 8:19, where fasts are to become feasts of joy, and in 2 Kings 20:19.

decisions.choice: 127 provinces
decisions.reason: The extent of Ahasuerus's empire, from India to Cush, as in 1:1 and 8:9.

decisions.choice: Mordecai
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the sender, following m1.

source.text: לְקַיֵּ֡ם אֵת־יְמֵי֩ הַפֻּרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ קִיַּ֨ם עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם מָרְדֳּכַ֤י הַיְּהוּדִי֙ וְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֛ר קִיְּמ֥וּ עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖ם וְעַל־זַרְעָ֑ם דִּבְרֵ֥י הַצֹּמ֖וֹת וְזַעֲקָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: to confirm [the] days of the Purim the these in their appointed times, as had established on them Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen, and as they had established on themselves and on their offspring, [the] matters of the fasts and their cry.

en.L: to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had established for themselves and for their descendants the matters of the fasts and their crying out.
en.B: to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had ordered them, and as they had taken on themselves and their descendants the keeping of fasts and lamenting.
en.R: to make the days of Purim official, to be kept at the right times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had commanded. The Jews had already agreed to this for themselves and their descendants, just as they had agreed to keep times of fasting and mourning.

decisions.choice: as they had established ... the matters of the fasts: the feast compared with fasts already kept
alternatives: the letter also fixed the fasts and laments that go with Purim
decisions.reason: The last words are hard to fit into the sentence. Most likely they mean that the Jews took on the feast of Purim just as they had already taken on days of fasting and mourning; it may instead mean that the letter also set rules for fasting along with the feast.

decisions.choice: the fasts and their cry
decisions.reason: The book has told of fasting and loud crying when Haman's decree went out (4:1-3) and of Esther's three-day fast (4:16). Jewish practice later kept a fast on the thirteenth of Adar, the day before Purim.

decisions.choice: fasting and mourning
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the matters of the fasts and their cry", a cry of distress as in 4:1-3. Readable folds this into "fasting and mourning" and, like the book itself, does not name God.

records.literal_gloss: And [the] command of Esther confirmed [the] matters of the Purim the these, and it was written in the book.

en.L: And the command of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.
en.B: Esther's command confirmed these rules for Purim, and it was written down in the book.
en.R: Esther's command made these rules for Purim official, and it was written down in a book.

decisions.choice: the matters of Purim: the rules for keeping Purim
decisions.reason: The word means words or matters; here, what Esther's letter laid down.

decisions.choice: written in the book: in a written record
decisions.reason: The text does not say which book. It may be a book of records, like the royal chronicles of 2:23, 6:1 and 10:2, or a scroll containing these rules.
